I personally never cared for the 3D TV. My main issue with it was how expensive it was to buy one and how little support you got for all the money you would have sank into the product.

3D TVs had a few problems:

  1. The expense. For most the extra cost was not justified.

  2. You have to wear glasses. It's not something people like to do. It's even worse for people who already have glasses.

  3. There wasn't enough compelling content. They had one really popular movie, which was Avatar. Other than that there were few things to truly draw people in.

  4. Some people had problems seeing the 3D effect.
Thank god. I was never into the 3d thing. Even 3d movies are pretty blegh to me, at some point I tune out and it's just like watching a normal movie anyhow.
I have a 3D TV. The glasses would never work. I don't even try to watch it in 3D because I have one movie that supports it. If it actually worked, maybe it would have taken off.

Virtual reality is the future of 3D. 3D is a gimmick that, for some reason, still makes enough money to be viable for new release movies. They've hit a dead-end with 3D, where the only real improvement in its history was moving from those horrible red and blue paper glasses to the clear plastic ones that we use now. VR has much more room for improvement and is far more immersive than classic 3D could ever be.
